transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We've got fourteen 55-gallon drums of spent coolant from the machining area staged in the waste staging area on spill pallets, and the disposal vendor still hasn't received their authorization. Before I can approve the disposal route and shipment controls, I need to run the round-robin review with lab quality, waste logistics, and warehouse supervision per our waste-authorization routine. Can we get that review scheduled so we can move this forward?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, before we schedule the round-robin review, I need to flag something critical. My laboratory analysis on these drums — completed yesterday but not yet attached to the waste authorization — found 2.4% chlorinated solvent in the spent coolant. Our waste matrix requires that any batch at or above 1.0% chlorinated solvent be routed to hazardous-liquid treatment rather than ordinary coolant recycling. These drums exceed that threshold, so the disposal route and shipment controls will need to reflect hazardous-liquid handling instead of standard coolant recycling.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, before we finalize the shipment controls, I need to flag something from the disposal contractor's service email that I haven't yet entered into the transport booking system. The contractor's tanker permit restricts us to no more than 8 of these drums per load, so the 14 drums will have to go out as two separate shipments — one load of 8 and a second load of 6. That permit condition needs to be factored into the disposal route and shipment controls we approve.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Elena, before we finalize the disposal route and shipment controls, I need to flag something from my warehouse inspection that I recorded on the shift clipboard but haven't yet updated in the waste file. I found active seepage at the base of exactly 4 of the 14 drums. Those 4 drums must be placed in UN-rated overpacks before any movement. The other 10 drums are fine to remain on their existing spill pallets. This overpack requirement needs to be factored into the shipment controls we approve.
transcript.speaker: A4
